source.title: Two Facets of SDE Under an Information-Theoretic Lens: Generalization of SGD via Training Trajectories and via Terminal States

record.file_problem: none; full paper and supplementary material supplied
record.tranche_reason: Empirically compares SGD and its SDE approximation on classifier testing performance and examines how derived bounds track generalization error. It does not test the claim versions' specified interventions or measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper's experiments report SGD/SDE performance comparisons and bound-versus-generalization-error results. Prior-work results mentioned in the text are not extracted as rows. Figure values are not numerically recoverable from the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The study tests SGD–SDE agreement and information-theoretic generalization bounds, but none of V1–V8. Its geometric bound and Hessian measurements do not measure magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance or its ranking of generalization gaps as specified by V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors report SGD–SDE agreement, a tighter trajectory-based bound than Wang and Mao (2022), and a geometry-dependent terminal-state bound that captures observed generalization-error trends better than their norm bounds. Terminal-state bounds appear to decay faster, but require additional assumptions, and the empirical bound estimates omit R.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SGD and a Gaussian-noise discrete SDE approximation to compare classifier performance and evaluate information-theoretic bounds; does not reproduce the interventions or measures in the listed original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning-rate changes at iterations 40,000 and 60,000 affected the measured gradient-based quantities. Training-sample size was varied in bound comparisons.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report similar performance dynamics for SGD and its discrete Gaussian-noise SDE approximation across four classifier–dataset settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Discrete SDE training approximates SGD performance dynamics in these VGG-11 and ResNet-18 experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report that their trajectory bound improves on Wang and Mao (2022), while their geometry-dependent terminal-state bound captures generalization-error trends better than the tested norm bounds. Estimates omit the variance proxy R.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed SDE-based bounds characterize aspects of generalization in the tested sample-size comparisons, with terminal-state bounds appearing to decay faster.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence
record.problems: The performance and bound comparisons are presented in figures without recoverable numerical values in the supplied text. Bound estimates exclude the subgaussian variance proxy R and therefore are not the true bound orders. The generalization-error estimates use limited samples in some measurements; gradient-covariance estimates use 100 training and 100 testing samples, and Hessian estimates use 100 training samples. Experiments use ten random seeds with fixed model initialization.
record.rows_left_out: No separately described results beyond R1–R7 meet the row rule. Cited results from other work and theoretical bounds without experimental outcomes are omitted.

untested.parts: Matched random-label memorization and natural-label held-out performance, including chance performance on random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that mitigate them; batch size is ordinarily fixed at 100 here.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and removal of dropout with weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps at similarly low training loss, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and measuring retrained test accuracy. The theoretical leave-one-out analysis does not test this intervention.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's tests/T2 classification conflicts with its correct assessment that every version is untested. States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8; this does not negate the authors' qualitative reports of SGD–SDE agreement.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under the same recipes.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Large versus small batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
